title: Slice ownership rotations and fallback scripts (wip)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working doc describing a lightweight operational pattern for rotating slice ownership during canary/A-B rollouts and standardizing automated fallback scripts. Goal: reduce cognitive load on on-call/product stewards, speed decision-making during anomalies, and make rollback/failover predictable and repeatable across teams.

Scope and constraints:
- Applies to console-driven canaries (phased exposure), experiment-driven A/B tests, and fast microreleases that live behind feature flags.
- Assumes telemetry from Redwood Console (per-route latency, token-cost, error-rate, user-visible regressions) and access to model-level metrics (p95-gen-latency, decode-errors).
- This pattern is operational, not experiment-design — it complements existing hypothesis & analysis docs.

High-level pattern (1-paragraph):
Assign a rotating "slice steward" (owner) for each active cohort/slice during an exposure window. The steward is the single point to execute pre-authorized fallback scripts (automated switch of traffic, model variant swap, or temporary 100% abort) and to coordinate cross-team comms. Ownership rotates in fixed cadence (4h blocks for day cadence or 24h for long tests). Each steward has a collapsible runbook + one-click scripts available in the rollout console.

Responsibilities (quick bullets):
- Slice steward: monitor slice dashboard, confirm signal thresholds, run fallback script when required, update incident log.
- Backup steward: notified immediately if primary steward is unreachable; authorized to act with the same scripts.
- Platform on-call: provides infra-level quick fixes (scale, capacity) but does NOT change slice-level hypothesis.
- Product owner / Experiment owner: owns metric interpretation and post-hoc decisions.

Rotation schedule (example):
- Weekdays: 08:00–20:00 local — 4h rotations, 3 stewards on call in overlapping windows (hand-off 15 mins).
- Night/Weekend: single 24h steward on rotation, backup on pager.
- Rapid microreleases: explicit steward assigned for the release window (start/end times in ticket).
Note: exact cadence to be tuned by team. Start with conservative 4h for first two months.

Eligibility & permissions checklist (pre-release):
- Steward has RBAC to run pre-approved scripts in Console or CLI (no ad-hoc infra changes).
- Steward listed in rollout ticket and accepted pager duty.
- Backup steward acknowledged.
- Playbook shortlink present in rollout ticket.

Defining slices (practical rules):
- Use easy-to-identify slices (logged as experiment cohort id or route prefix). Avoid high-cardinality user segmentation for stewarding.
- Examples: 1% new users in EU (slice: eu-new-1pct), logged search requests for reranker tests (slice: reranker-q1).
- Each slice has a minimal telemetry set: request-rate, p95 latency, surface error-rate (API 5xx), model-quality signal (eval proxy or flagged outputs).

Gating metrics & thresholds (starter):
- Sev thresholds (auto-fail): request error rate > 2% sustained for 3 minutes OR p95 latency degraded > 2x baseline for 5 minutes.
- Quality signals (manual fail/rollback triggers): negative NPS proxy up by +30% on cohort compared to baseline OR automated eval drop > 8% on golden set.
- Cost spike: per-token spend > 150% of expected burn for two consecutive 10m windows -> alert steward, recommended partial rollback.
- Observability: Console should surface deltas vs baseline and absolute values; steward always checks both.

Automated fallback scripts (standardized set) — examples and safe defaults:
Note: scripts must be idempotent and produce a signed audit log entry. All scripts are additive (no manual DB/infra mutation) and revert to a known-good configuration.
1) revert-to-stable.sh (DEFAULT) — switches traffic for slice -> baseline model variant (no config change).
   - Inputs: slice-id, reason-code, ticket-id
   - Outputs: Console response (new allocation) and audit event
2) reduce-exposure.sh — halves exposure percentage for slice (e.g., 1% -> 0.5%).
3) pause-feature-flag.sh — toggles flag to OFF for flag-backed releases (must require 2FA confirmation).
4) emergency-abort.sh — immediate 100% traffic cut for slice (must be used only if severity auto-fail hit).

Example pseudo-script (for docs, not actual executable):
#!/usr/bin/env bash
SLICE=$1
TICKET=$2
REASON=$3
# idempotent switch to stable variant
curl -X POST $CONSOLE_API/traffic/switch -d "{"slice":"$SLICE","target":"stable","ticket":"$TICKET","reason":"$REASON"}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# exit codes: 0 success, 2 partial applied, 3 fail -> page SRE

Pre-authorization & governance:
- Product + SRE sign-off on allowed fallback scripts before experiment starts. Document approval in ticket.
- Scripts have constrained API tokens (auditable) and require a reason-code and ticket reference.
- For emergency-abort, require either: (a) steward + backup OR (b) steward + platform on-call confirmation.

Comms templates (short) — to use in Slack incident channel: 
- Initial alert (auto-posted): "[Canary][slice-id] Deviation detected: p95 latency x2; steward @jordan assigned. Please stand by. Link: <ticket>"
- After fallback: "[Canary][slice-id] Fallback applied: revert-to-stable by @jordan. Reason: latency spike. See ticket <ticket>."

Post-action checklist (immediate):
- Steward annotates ticket with exact script run, inputs, and observed delta.
- Platform on-call confirms infra-level state (pods healthy, no OOMs).
- Product owner schedules post-mortem if quality signal triggered.

Post-release retrospective prompts (for experiment owner):
- Was rotation cadence adequate?
- Were thresholds tuned appropriately?
- Did fallback scripts behave idempotently?
- Any friction or missing RBAC gaps?

Open questions / TODOs:
- Tighten mobile-specific slices semantics (edge caches + offline UX impact).
- Build console UI affordance for one-click steward handover.
- Add audit-level verification that scripts cannot change infra beyond scoped APIs.
- Run 2 pilot rollouts with 4h cadence and collect steward feedback.

Notes and references:
- See RDW-1245 for prior incident that motivated rotation idea; infra PR linked above.
- Related playbooks: experiment-safety-corridor, staggered-release-playbook (confluence references).

Quick link list (for inclusion in rollout ticket):
- playbook: Confluence:/rollouts/slice-ownership-policy
- scripts repo: GH:github.com/redwood/ops/rollout-scripts
- ticket template: JIRA:RDW-EXPERIMENT-TEMPLATE
